title: A figure with two decimal points is no number in verify
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/desk/verify.ts lex() read "4.0.5" as two juxtaposed numbers and the parser multiplied them, so a typed answer, a second go or a photographed read with two decimal points could mark "right".

## Description
lex (desk/src/lib/desk/verify.ts:40-47) took digits, one optional ".digits", and stopped; the next "." began a new number token (desk/src/lib/desk/verify.ts:48-53), and term() multiplies juxtaposed atoms (desk/src/lib/desk/verify.ts:102-103). substitute("x+1=3","4.0.5") was true. This is the deterministic backstop every linear verdict rests on (registry judgment-guardbands / deterministic-backbone: the backbone must not be moved by malformed input). Fixed: a second decimal point after a number is no figure (lex returns null), so the value is unreadable and the item stays unsure.

## Flow
- phone: type "4.0.5" for x+1=3 -> /api/mark typed -> markTyped -> judgeItem -> substitute -> true -> verdict right (before)
- fix: lex refuses "." directly after a number with a decimal part, and after a leading-dot number
- after: substitute -> null -> verdict unsure, secondGo null (the go is not spent)

## Expected impact
A learner who mistypes a value with two points is asked, not told "right"; skill estimates stop taking false rights. Could break: a source that writes a trailing sentence period after a decimal ("1.5.") - already null before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a malformed figure never decides a verdict
Before: 4 of 4 two-point values substitute true (x+1=3 "4.0.5", 2x=5 "5.0.5", x-1=0 "2.0.5"; ".4.5" evaluated); markTyped verdict right, secondGo right
After: 4 of 4 null; markTyped unsure; secondGo null; "2.0", "2." and ".5x" unchanged
Method: gate - maths-rules-test gate case 2b red then green; 6 more suites that load verify.ts green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/verify.ts:43 `if (s[j] === ".") { j++; ...digits }` then a new token at :48 for the next "."
probe: substitute("x+1=3","4.0.5") -> true; evaluate("4.0.5",0) -> 2; markTyped(["4.0.5"]) -> ["right"]

title: The analyse route refuses a body that is not a reading
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts read its body with a bare req.json(): a non-JSON or null body threw (500), and a body with no kind, an unknown kind or no text started an analyse job that failed on a TypeError and told the TV "Try again".

## Description
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:26 `const body = (await req.json()) as Body` - the only route of the seven here without a parse guard. A kind-less body fell to the essay branch (desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:112-124) and ran analyseEssay(undefined); "english" with no sentence ran analyseSentence(undefined). Each wrote job.failed and the status line "The desk could not read that through. Try again." - a Try again that can never succeed (registry error-handling / user-facing-mapping). Fixed: KINDS list, a 400 in desk words for a missing kind or blank text, before any run.

## Flow
- POST /api/analyse "{}" with a learner seated -> runJob analyse -> splitSentences(undefined) throws -> job.failed, TV status "Try again" (before)
- POST "not json" / "null" -> unhandled throw -> 500 (before)
- after: 400 NOT_A_READING, no job, no model call

## Expected impact
The TV no longer shows a failure a learner did not cause; a stray client cannot overwrite the analyse job record. Could break: a caller sending a kind-less essay body - none found (phone, tv/keys.ts, 5 suites all send kind).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - malformed input is refused at the door, never a failed job
Before: 11 of 11 malformed bodies reach a throw (2) or a started analyse job (9)
After: 11 of 11 answer 400 in desk words, no job, no model call
Method: gate - essay-rules-test new case red then green; essay-piece, learner-switch, voice-rules, week-digest green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:26 `const body = (await req.json()) as Body;`
probe: "{}" -> 502 + job failed "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')"; "null" -> THROW TypeError; "not json" -> THROW SyntaxError

title: essay-rules-test keeps its data directory in the OS temp dir and removes it
body:
## Summary
tools/essay-rules-test.cjs put DESK_DATA_DIR inside the tree (artifacts/essay-rules/<ms>) and never removed it, against the overlay repo law; 198 such directories sit in the main checkout.

## Description
tools/essay-rules-test.cjs:10 set DESK_DATA_DIR=path.resolve(__dirname,"../artifacts/essay-rules",Date.now()) and its after() (tools/essay-rules-test.cjs:58) only cleared the ticker. The overlay says a test that needs learner data sets DESK_DATA_DIR under the OS temp dir; the other three suites of this context (maths-rules, desk-jobs-rules, withhold-rules) do. Fixed: mkdtemp under os.tmpdir(), rmSync in after(), and a GUARD case pinning the directory under tmpdir.

## Flow
- run essay-rules-test -> artifacts/essay-rules/<ms>/learners.json left behind (before)
- after: desk-essay-rules-* in temp, removed at the end

## Expected impact
git status and the tree stop collecting a directory per run (gitignored, but litter a sweep cannot tell from work). The 198 old directories in the main checkout are not removed by this commit - operator housekeeping.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - test hygiene against a stated repo rule
Before: 1 directory left inside the tree per run; 3 of 4 suites here follow the rule; 198 accumulated in C:/Users/kazda/kiro/firetv/artifacts/essay-rules
After: 0 left in the tree and 0 in temp per run; 4 of 4 suites follow the rule
Method: gate - GUARD case red on the old path, green now; essay-rules-test 130 pass
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Tonight's memory lines are written in one save (WD10)
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts wrote each memory line with its own addMemory save; a write failing part way kept some lines while the job failed, and Try again appended them again.

## Description
WD10 is the rule that a run's record changes go in ONE save (desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts route: desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:188, desk/src/lib/desk/mark.ts:357-373, desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:117-125). writeMemory looped `for (const l of lines) addMemory(learnerId, l)` - up to three read-modify-writes of learners.json. Fixed: the lines are appended to a freshly read learner in one saveLearner.

## Flow
- End session -> /api/memory -> writeMemory -> 3 lines -> 3 learners.json writes (before)
- the 2nd write fails -> job failed, 1 line kept -> Try again -> the model writes 3 lines again -> line 1 twice (before)
- after: one write; a failure keeps none

## Expected impact
The learner's notes stop collecting duplicates after a failed evening write. learners.ts addMemory now has no production caller (tests only; not this context's file).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed save writes all or nothing
Before: 3 learners.json writes for 3 lines; a failure on the 2nd write kept 1 of 3
After: 1 write; a failure keeps 0 of 3
Method: gate - desk-jobs-rules case 6b red then green; calc-marking, econ-rules, linga-rules, tv-recap green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts (before) `for (const l of lines) addMemory(learnerId, l);`
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:380-386 addMemory = getLearner + saveLearner per call
case 6b before: "three lines, one write of learners.json" actual 3

title: The essay lens maps are keyed by the lens ids, with no silent Structure fallback
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts held DECIDING, OBSERVED and OBSERVE as Record<string, ...> with `?? <map>.structure`: a lens added to rules/essay ANALYSIS_TYPES without entries here compiled and was read with Structure's field.

## Description
The three hand-maintained maps (desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:25-37) were never checked against the ground truth, ANALYSIS_TYPES (desk/src/lib/rules/essay.ts:204-210). §4.7: what enumerates the ground truth? Nothing did. Fixed: Record<AnalysisType, ...> on all three, fallbacks removed; essay-rules E7-7 pins the typing and forbids the fallback (it pinned the old expression, §7.5).

## Flow
- add a fifth lens to ANALYSIS_TYPES without OBSERVE/OBSERVED/DECIDING entries -> tsc green, the reading asks Structure's job field (before)
- after: tsc TS2741 names the missing key

## Expected impact
A future lens cannot ship half-wired. No prompt or schema changed for the four lenses (E7-7 per-lens required fields hold).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the compiler enumerates the lens list
Before: seeded control (delete OBSERVE.language) -> tsc exit 0; 3 silent fallbacks
After: same seed -> tsc TS2741 (red); E7-7 seeded back to Record<string> -> red; 0 fallbacks
Method: gate - tsc seeded both sides; essay-rules 130 pass, essay-piece, voice-rules, week-digest green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:25 `const DECIDING: Record<string, string>`; :38 `OBSERVED[lens.id] ?? OBSERVED.structure`; :42 `DECIDING[lens.id] ?? DECIDING.structure`; :85 `OBSERVE[lens.id] ?? OBSERVE.structure`

title: A job's onFail that throws reaches the server log
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts swallowed an onFail that threw with an empty catch: the put-right could break and no door saw it.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:114 `try { opts.onFail?.(e); } catch {}` - the runner's one swallowed catch (registry error-handling / error-doors: every failure reaches at least one door; swallowed-error-prevention). read uses onFail to stop the page "reading"; if it threw, the session stayed half put right in silence. Fixed: one console.error line (kind, run id, first line, 120 chars - the same detail rule as the run's own line, never a screen).

## Flow
- a run fails -> onFail throws -> catch {} -> nothing logged (before)
- after: "desk job onFail failed: <kind> <id>: <first line>" in the server log; the failure still recorded in desk words

## Expected impact
An operator can see why a screen kept saying "reading". Nothing user-facing changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - observability: swallowed paths counted
Before: 1 swallowed catch; a throwing onFail logs 0 lines about itself
After: 0 swallowed; 1 log line
Method: gate - desk-jobs-rules case 6c red then green; learner-switch green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The school system's notation sentence lives once, for the read and the hint
body:
## Summary
hint.ts groundFor carried its own copy of the notation sentence read.ts mathsContext writes, while its doc said it was "the wording of the maths read".

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts:32-36 and desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:194-197 (before) both built "The learner is in the <system> school system, whose notation uses <note>." from their own literal notes - two implementations of one wording (§4.6). A fix to one (a new system, a corrected cz note) would tell the hint model a different notation than the read model. Fixed: read.ts notationLine, called by both.

## Flow
- add a system or change the cz note in read.ts -> the hint keeps the old wording (before)
- after: one function, both prompts

## Expected impact
No prompt changed today (hash below); the two prompts cannot drift.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one wording for one rule
Before: 2 copies of the template, 4 literal notes
After: 1 copy (notationLine); sha256 of 20 prompt strings (uk/us/cz/de/none x 2 problems) c4a3466d... identical before and after
Method: probe - prompt strings hashed on both sides; no test can pin a duplicate count more cheaply; 11 suites + tsc green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts (before) `const note = who.system === "cz" ? "a decimal comma (3,5), division written with a colon, and tg and cotg for tan and cot" : ...`

title: A piece sent to be kept while a reading runs is refused before it is kept
body:
## Summary
The piece branch of desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts kept the learner's text on their shelf before runJob's one-at-a-time check: a send refused 409 had already kept a piece, and every press added another.

## Description
addPiece/addVersion ran at desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:87-94 (before), runJob's blocksRun only at :97. addPiece does not dedupe (desk/src/lib/session/texts.ts:93-103), so each refused press added a duplicate toward TEXT_PIECES_MAX. Fixed: blocksRun asked before the keep - the same rule runJob applies.

## Flow
- a reading is running -> the phone sends a piece with keep -> addPiece -> runJob 409 BUSY (before: piece kept)
- press again -> another piece kept (before)
- after: 409 before the keep, shelf unchanged

## Expected impact
The learner's shelf holds only pieces that were read. Could break: nothing - a free desk keeps and reads as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a refused request has no side effect
Before: 2 refused sends while a reading runs -> 2 pieces kept
After: 0 kept, 409 each
Method: gate - essay-rules new case red then green; essay-piece, learner-switch, voice-rules, week-digest, texts-rules, phone-panel, twin-rules green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: analyse essay held running; POST piece keep:true -> 409 "The desk is already on it."; listPieces("ema") 0 -> 1

title: A snapped page whose title is not text is read under the desk's own title
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts took body.title as given: a number or object broke the learner history write and the desk said READ_NOT_SAVED, a disk failure that never happened.

## Description
`title: body.title ?? "Page"` (desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:22, before) covered only undefined/null. A number reached withHistory's label.trim() (desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts withHistory), which threw inside the learner write's try (desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:184-192): no history line, no digest entry, and a false "could not write it to the learner file". A blank title wrote no history line. Fixed: a non-text or blank title is "Page".

## Flow
- POST /api/read {title: 42} -> page lands -> saveLearner throws "e.label?.trim is not a function" -> saved false -> READ_NOT_SAVED (before)
- after: saved true, one history line "Page"

## Expected impact
No false disk-failure line; the week digest counts the read. Could break: nothing; the phone always sends a string.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a stated failure is a real one
Before: title 42 / object -> saved false, 0 history lines, READ_NOT_SAVED said, page.title 42
After: 3 of 3 non-text titles -> saved true, 1 history line "Page", page.title "Page"
Method: gate - desk-jobs-rules case 6d red then green; desk-pairing, week-digest, learner-switch green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: title 42 -> 200 {saved:false,learnerSaved:false}; log "desk read: the page was read but could not be written to the learner file: e.label?.trim is not a function"

title: A hint question that is not text or is over the cap is refused before any run
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/api/hint/route.ts took askedQ of any type and length into the prompt, session.hint (saved and streamed) and the job input; every other free-text door here is typed and capped.

## Description
The explain transcript has EXPLAIN_TRANSCRIPT_MAX (desk/src/lib/rules/saidValue.ts:12), typed answers TYPED_ANSWER_MAX (desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:106), the essay paragraph and piece their own caps; the hint question (desk/src/app/api/hint/route.ts:22,48,50) had none, and store.ts documents JobInput as never anything big. title: A JSON null body is no throw on read, hint, explain and retry

title: A memory note the learner already holds is written again
instrument: desk-jobs-rules case "a memory line the notes already hold - or said twice tonight - is not written again" (writeMemory twice with an overlapping stub), plus tools/tv-recap-test.cjs M2 given a fresh second line; decided by both suites green
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts appends every model line, including one the learner's notes already hold or one repeated in the same answer; the prompt asks for no repeat, code never checks.

## Description
The prompt says "do not repeat any of it" (desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:64) but the lines are stored as returned (:68-74). With MEMORY_CAP 40 the duplicates push real notes out and are read back into every explain and practice prompt. Built and green in desk-jobs (case red then green), then reverted: tools/tv-recap-test.cjs M2 (another context, edited in flight by another agent this wave) stubs the SAME line twice and expects the route's `lines` to echo it - the change also redefines /api/memory `lines` as "what tonight added".

## Flow
- writeMemory returns "They undo the constant first." when the notes hold it -> stored twice (before)
- fix: drop a line equal (case, runs of space) to a held note or to an earlier line of the same answer; update tv-recap M2's stub

## Expected impact
Notes stay distinct; the phone's "What the desk noticed" shows only new lines. Could break: a consumer that expects the raw model lines back.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stored notes are distinct
Before: a held note returned again -> stored twice (desk-jobs case red: memory deepEqual failed)
After: stored once; desk-jobs green; tv-recap M2 red until its stub changes
Method: gate - built in this round, reverted for the coupled out-of-context test (veto 4: tv-recap-test.cjs in flight)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:68-74 lines filtered for type and blank only
tools/tv-recap-test.cjs:298 expects lines ["They undo the constant first once they see it."] on a learner whose notes already hold it

title: Explain's reply leak check is a per-kind subset of the hint's leaksLine
instrument: a withhold-rules case that runs explainItem's gate (leaks | leaksCalc | leaksSchool by kind) and hint.ts leaksLine over one corpus - the 24 recorded hint stages, generated school sets (makeSchoolItems over every unit, seed fixed) and Calculus specs, each with lines stating the answer in figures, words and cz notation - and counts lines one passes and the other stops
body:
## Summary
The hint and the lesson-pick "why" pass hint.ts leaksLine (the one leak rule OR each reader's own); the explain reply, also shown on the TV caption, passes only its kind's check.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts (explainItem) `gives = calc ? leaksCalc(...) : school ? leaksSchool(...) : leaks(...)`; desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts leaksLine = leaks || leaksCalc || leaksSchool || parts; desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts checkedWhy uses leaksLine and its doc calls it "like every hint line". A Calculus or school reply never meets the general rule, and a multi-part item's siblings are never checked. No line has yet been shown that one passes and the other stops.

## Flow
- explain on a school item: reply states the value in a form leaksSchool misses but leaks reads -> shown (predicted)
- fix: explainItem gates with leaksLine(question, specs of the item, reply, system)

## Expected impact
Withholding on the explain caption equals the hint's. Could break: a method line leaks() over-reads on a Calculus item, replaced by the item's own line.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one leak rule on every model line put on screen
Before: 3 checkers by kind at explain vs 1 combined at hint and pick; differing lines on a corpus: not counted
After: the instrument's count of lines the explain gate passes and leaksLine stops
Method: simulation - the corpus instrument is M and was not built this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts leaksLine; desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:234 checkedWhy -> leaksLine; desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts explainItem `const gives = calc ? leaksCalc(item.spec, h.reply) : school ? leaksSchool(item.spec, h.reply) : leaks(item.question, h.reply, system);`
ab_figures: explainItem stops 949 of 983 lines vs leaksLine stops 949, 0 differ (95 items)

title: A failed lesson (teach) holds its input but Try again cannot reach it
instrument: a desk-jobs case: /api/worked fails with a stubbed text engine -> POST /api/session/retry {kind:"teach"} -> expect the same topic re-asked through /api/worked; plus the phone or TV offering it (phone-surface / tv-surface)
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/api/worked/route.ts records `input: { topic }` on the teach job so it "can be asked again in place", but desk/src/app/api/session/retry/route.ts ROUTES holds only read, hint and practice, and no screen offers Try again for a lesson.

## Description
retry ROUTES (desk/src/app/api/session/retry/route.ts:17-21) is a hand list over JobKind; teach is the one kind that stores an input without a retry path (worked/route.ts:26). The context promise is "try again in place". Either the input is dead weight or the retry is missing; the screens that would offer it are in other contexts.

## Flow
- the lesson write fails -> job teach failed with input {topic} -> POST /api/session/retry {kind:"teach"} -> 409 "There is nothing to try again." (today)
- fix: add teach to ROUTES -> worked POST; offer Try again where the failure shows

## Expected impact
A failed lesson can be asked again in place like a failed set. Could break: a retry while a newer lesson runs (runJob refuses 409).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every failed run with an input can be asked again
Before: 3 of 4 kinds that store an input are retryable
After: 4 of 4
Method: simulation - walked from the code; the worked route and the screens are outside this context
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/session/retry/route.ts:17 `ROUTES ... read, hint, practice`
desk/src/app/api/worked/route.ts:26 `{ key: topic, input: { topic }, ... }`

title: The Linga sentence and the snapped photo have no server-side size cap
instrument: two route cases: POST /api/analyse {kind:"english", sentence: 100k chars} and POST /api/read with a 30 MB data URL -> expect 400 in desk words with no job and no engine call; caps as constants in rules/english (linga) and rules/maths or a read rule
body:
## Summary
analyse kind "english" sends any length of sentence to the model, and read takes a photo of any size into the session (persisted, streamed) and the vision engine; the phone downsizes, the server does not check.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts english branch runs analyseSentence(body.sentence) with no length rule (the essay branch has essayTooLong, the piece pieceProblem, explain EXPLAIN_TRANSCRIPT_MAX, hint HINT_QUESTION_MAX now). desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:21-29 checks presence and size fields only; the phone resizes to JPEG 0.85 (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:195) but any client may post more. The sentence cap belongs in rules/english (linga context).

## Flow
- POST /api/analyse {kind:"english", sentence: 100k chars} -> one model call on it (predicted)
- POST /api/read with a 30 MB image -> stored on the page, written to session.json, sent to vision (predicted)

## Expected impact
Bounded cost and session size per request. Could break: a legitimate large photo - the cap must sit above what the phone produces.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every door capped
Before: 2 doors uncapped of 8 text/image doors in this context
After: 0 uncapped
Method: simulation - walked from the code; the sentence cap is linga's rules file, the image cap needs a measured phone ceiling
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts english branch: no cap before runJob
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:23 `img: body.image ?? ""` - presence only
